title: STYLE OUTWEIGHS SUBSTANCE: FAILURE MODES OF LLM JUDGES IN ALIGNMENT BENCHMARKING

bias_targets.methodology: Applying systematic stylistic alterations (e.g., making text bland, concise, sarcastic, or undiverse) to model responses using GPT-4o-mini, and measuring how these changes impact the overall preference scores given by LLM judges.

Prompting LLM judges to provide scores on explicit fine-grained criteria (completeness, conciseness, style, safety, correctness) alongside an overall preference score, and using correlation and factor analysis to reveal how judges disproportionately weight style over factuality and safety.

Appending irrelevant but verified academic references or mimicking GPT-4 generated citations (reference stuffing) to model responses to test if the LLM judge artificially boosts scores based on the mere presence of authoritative formatting.
